nodes.description: The initiating lesion. Nine missense variants are known, all in the mature protein rather than the mitochondrial targeting presequence, and most lie in the last exon. Arg360 is changed in three unrelated families (to Cys, Gly and Leu) and has been proposed as a mutational hotspot. Two complementation experiments in patient fibroblasts, carrying the Arg321Pro and Arg360Cys alleles, show that wild-type NDUFA9 corrects the defect. That makes the variants causal and loss of function.

genetic_context.description: Curated as loss of function because wild-type NDUFA9 rescues the fibroblast defect. The reported alleles are all missense, and the 2025 cohort authors suggest that complete loss of NDUFA9 may be incompatible with survival. If so, the human alleles are hypomorphs rather than nulls, but this has not been tested and PARTIAL_LOSS_OF_FUNCTION is not asserted. Zygosity is left unset at entry level because eleven of twelve patients are homozygous and one is compound heterozygous.

nodes.description:
NDUFA9 joins complex I early, as one of the Q-module matrix-arm subunits (with NDUFS2 and NDUFS3) in the roughly 400 kDa intermediate that contains ND1 and the NDUFAF3/NDUFAF4 assembly factors. This is the intermediate that fails to form in MC1DN18 (NDUFAF3). Its essential job, though, comes late. Human cells lacking NDUFA9 build a membrane-arm subcomplex that has no matrix arm attached, which places NDUFA9 at the junction that holds the two arms together.
Patient fibroblasts show the same failure. Fully assembled complex I is reduced and Q-module subassemblies accumulate. In the most severely affected patient, P-module subassemblies accumulate as well, and in one 2025 patient a stalled, partially assembled intermediate was seen. Re-expressing wild-type NDUFA9 corrects assembly both in knockout cells and in patient cells.

All five patients tested had complex I deficiency in fibroblasts and/or muscle, and the deficiency is isolated: the other respiratory chain complexes are normal in both amount and activity. Residual activity ranges from about 2 percent of control in the fatal neonatal case to about 20 percent in the two adults with dystonia. nodes.description:
How a single amino-acid change in an accessory subunit could weaken the enzyme. Structural modelling on the human complex I structure predicts two kinds of damage. Most variants replace a positively charged arginine or lysine. Some of these break ion pairs, which leads to misfolding. The Arg360 variants instead remove a residue that binds negatively charged membrane phospholipids, and that binding is how NDUFA9 anchors the hydrophilic domain to the membrane. Steady-state NDUFA9 protein was reduced in fibroblasts from two brothers homozygous for Arg354Gln, but was normal in a compound heterozygote (Arg360Gly/Gly267Val) who still lost assembled complex I. So reduced protein is not the only route to disease.
Marked PROVISIONAL because the misfolding and phospholipid-binding consequences come from in silico modelling and have not been measured for any variant.

nodes.description: The Leigh syndrome lesion pattern, and the substrate of the movement disorder. Every patient imaged had abnormal basal ganglia signal, always involving the putamen and caudate. The accumbens, thalami and globi pallidi were involved less often. Atrophy or swelling and foci of restricted diffusion accompany the signal change, and symmetric brainstem lesions (central tegmental tracts, cerebral peduncles, periaqueductal grey, posterior medulla) appear in a minority. Follow-up scans in two brothers showed the basal ganglia atrophy getting worse. The 2025 authors read the consistency of the striatal involvement as a selective vulnerability of these structures. The cause of that vulnerability is not known.
